title: Kissing number in dimension 21, lower bound
statement: Find as many nonzero vectors as possible in R^21 with pairwise angles of at least 60 degrees (unit spheres centred at twice the normalised vectors then all touch a central unit sphere without overlapping); k such vectors show that the kissing number in dimension 21 is at least k. The best known configuration, by K. Li (2026), has 31560 vectors; one with more vectors improves it. Some of the best known configurations in dimensions 17 to 21 need irrational coordinates, so they cannot be given here as integer vectors.
submission: Text file: one vector per line, integer coordinates separated by spaces or commas, all with the same squared norm N; more than 21 coordinates are allowed when the vectors span a space of dimension at most 21. Every inner product between two vectors must be at most N/2.
score: k, the number of vectors (larger is better)

best_known.source: kissing number in dimension 21 >= 31560: K. Li (2026), in Henry Cohn's table of kissing numbers (cohn.mit.edu/kissing-numbers) and Leaps in Bounds (github.com/daniel-munro/leaps-in-bounds), data at commit 4521e13 (8 Nov 2026); read 8 Nov 2026
